text:
**Short answer:** Pick a station with at least 1,800 W of continuous AC output. Inverter wattage matters more than battery size here. A single-burner induction plate draws up to about 1,800 W on high ([HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/induction-cooktop/)). An electric kettle is a similar high-watt load, so the same rule covers it.

**My pick: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (about $899)**
- It has a 2,600 W inverter and 2,073.6 Wh of capacity. That gives headroom at full power and enough energy for days of cooking ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop)).
- Stations rated exactly 1,800 W, such as the BLUETTI AC180 and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus, run a plate right at its limit. Many cheap plates also pulse at 1,200 W even on low, so the extra margin helps ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop)).
- Buy link: [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). That page says the code DEALECTRIC saves $44.95 and is pre-applied by the link. Dealectric is the seller, so that is a retailer claim.

**Budget or bigger options**
- **DJI Power 1000:** HomePowerFacts calls it the smallest station it tracks that can run a single-burner induction cooktop. Expect only about 0.4 h at full power ([HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/induction-cooktop/)). It suits short cooking sessions or lower power settings.
- **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (4,096 Wh) or DELTA Pro Ultra:** These give the longest runtimes. The DELTA Pro 3 lasts about 3 hours ([Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/induction-cooktop)). The DELTA Pro Ultra also lasts about 3 hours on full power ([HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/induction-cooktop/)). They cost much more, and I didn't see prices in these results.

**Stations to avoid for this**
- Small units can't run it. The EcoFlow RIVER 3 and RIVER 2 are limited to 300 W continuous. The RIVER 3 Plus, BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 and Jackery Explorer 300 v2 also can't ([HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/induction-cooktop/), [Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/induction-cooktop)).
- The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 stops at 1,500 W, so it will shut off if you turn the burner to high ([Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/induction-cooktop)).

**Runtime tips**
- Boiling a litre takes roughly 90–110 Wh. A one-pot meal at 1,200 W for 15 minutes is about 300 Wh ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop)). That works out to about eight boils or three to four meals per 1 kWh.
- Use high power to bring food up to temperature, then drop to 400–800 W to simmer. This can roughly halve the battery used ([PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/devices/induction-cooktop)).
- Heat is a factor. A station running near 1,500–1,800 W for long stretches gets warm and may cut output, so keep its vents clear ([VanLifeKitchens](https://vanlifekitchens.com/guides/can-a-power-station-run-an-induction-cooktop)).

Some of these sources are affiliate or retailer sites, and the runtimes come from calculations, not hands-on testing.
